title: 'Script timeout' / Infinite Yield Warnings
summary: 'Script timeout: exhausted' and 'Infinite yield possible on WaitForChild' mean a thread waited past its budget — usually WaitForChild on a wrong name, an event that never fires, or an endless while-true without task.wait.

explanation.whatItIs: The engine's smoke alarm for threads parked too long: something you waited for never arrived.
explanation.whyItExists: Unbounded waiting hides bugs forever; the warning surfaces them after ~5 seconds of suspicious yielding.
symptoms: 'Infinite yield possible on 'X:WaitForChild("Y")'' — usually wrong name or container
'Script timeout' after an Event:Wait() that never fired
Game 'hangs' — actually one thread parked, others may be fine
explanation.fix: Check the waited-for name/path (copy it from Explorer); add timeouts to WaitForChild; ensure the event you Wait() actually fires; add task.wait() to bare loops; verify the script SIDE (client waiting for server-only content).
tips: WaitForChild("Name", 5) + nil check turns hangs into diagnosable branches
Cross-check replication timing — maybe it arrives, just later than you wait
Event:Wait() inside a one-shot task.spawn keeps the main flow moving
commonMistakes: Waiting on the wrong universe (LocalScript waiting for ServerStorage content)
while true do with no task.wait() — busy loops choke the scheduler

examples.title: From hang to diagnosable
examples.code:
-- ❌ Can hang forever:
-- local shop = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shoppe")  -- typo!

-- ✅ Times out and tells you:
local shop = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Shoppe", 5)
if not shop then
    warn("Shoppe not found after 5s — check name/container")
end

-- ❌ Bare busy loop:
-- while true do checkSomething() end

-- ✅ Cooperative loop:
while true do
    checkSomething()
    task.wait(0.1)
end
